children.value: . We compute the finite polynomial’s Pauli coefficients, construct its actual PREPARE/SELECT/unprepare circuit, and measure a property of the accepted solution state. LCU supplies a quantum implementation of a linear combination; related quantum linear-system algorithms use other reciprocal expansions
. Our finite Neumann choice, exact coefficient aggregation and example are original.

A positive identity-dominant Hermitian Pauli matrix, a complex input circuit, a finite reciprocal polynomial, explicit access and ordinary known-input amplification are implemented. The analytic polynomial error is uniform across a specified interval. Tiny circuits are independently checked; larger generated circuits are marked separately. Classical Pauli aggregation is capped and can grow exponentially. General sparse matrix loading, a QSVT reciprocal phase compiler, certified hardware synthesis and Lean formalization remain unavailable.

children.value: Generation allows 24 data wires, 32 input terms, degree 64, 256 aggregate terms and 200,000 expanded primitive operations. Input rational numerators/denominators are capped at 512 bits, their normalized common denominator at 128 bits, literals at 192 characters and scientific exponents at magnitude 128. Reference solves allow six data wires and statevectors at most 12 total wires. Named large rows are circuit-only exports. The separate bounded physical study below covers selected size/gap cases; the larger logical grids remain unprojected.

children.value: includes input gates, every Pauli access, any complete source inverses/reflections, and all final measurements. Exact coefficient preprocessing and source generation/lowering CPU times are measured separately in one local run; these activities overlap in implementation and are not added as disjoint end-to-end timings.

For one Pauli mean, .03 statistical error and .005 statistical failure require 13,315 accepted samples. A separate .005 no-acceptance allowance sets the fresh-attempt cap. The default numerical success gives ten attempts per slot, or 133,150 capped full attempts. These are

. All rejected attempts pay the entire schedule. Amplified workloads use the checked prepared-input probability; the unamplified lower bound cannot be blindly substituted into the nonmonotone amplification formula.
supplies seven conditional Pareto points for the default unamplified task. It uses the existing illustrative
physical error rate, 100 ns gates/500 ns measurements, separate .005 physical-fault allowance over all attempts, and a
per-attempt synthesis-model allowance. Factory, distance, peak-qubit and serial-runtime results are in the report; the frozen Grover baseline is unchanged.
The analytic polynomial bound is not a hardware certificate.

The ledger separately bounds exact rational coefficient conversion to its floating values and reports a conversion-adjusted state bound in an otherwise exact-angle model. That coefficient-only correction does not certify numerical rotation construction or subsequent synthesis. The full numerical gate implementation and QDK’s mean-fit rotation model do not certify an operator norm, conditional mean, acceptance rate or actual synthesis sequence. Clean initialization timing/faults and classical reference/readout processing time are excluded. Physical runtime excludes the separately measured coefficient construction and compilation. Dependency depth is not a complete hardware schedule.

The pinned QASM exporter may omit an overall compiled global phase; the ledger records that phase. All exports are scoped to complete measured trials, rather than phase-preserving coherently controlled inverse oracles.

children.value: costs n=2,3,4 at promised gap 1/2, and n=2 at gaps 3/4,1/2,1/4,1/8. Degree is selected from a uniform 0.001 Pauli-bias ceiling: 4,9,24,51 across those gaps. All selected circuits and readout laws have independent small-instance checks. The HHL panels use different matrices and do not establish a matched algorithm-advantage comparison.

The common normalized-Z tolerance is 0.05: 0.01 algorithm bias, 0.01 postselection-adjusted synthesis bias and 0.03 sampling. Statistical, no-acceptance and physical-fault allowances are each 0.005, totaling 0.015 per separate case. There is no simultaneous guarantee across the grid. The profile is fixed at physical error

Every case charges all preparation, access, readout and rejected complete attempts. The uniform acceptance lower bound determines retries throughout; chosen-input numerical probabilities do not replace it. The

per-attempt QDK synthesis scalar is only hypothetically treated as a complete coherent error bound. No actual synthesis sequence or hardware-confidence certificate is supplied. Fresh logical-zero initialization/reset, classical preprocessing/readout, routing and decoder realization remain excluded.

Tests and independent reviews compare rational polynomial coefficients with separately assembled matrix powers, actual access blocks with the polynomial, and normalized accepted states with classical solves. They vary degree, conditioning, word width and complex inputs. Actual reflected circuits are checked against the amplitude formula and the unamplified accepted direction. X/Y/Z basis readout and invalid/oversized input rejection are covered. No Lean formalization or integrated synthesis theorem covers these gates.
